title: Vintage Bollywood
prompt:
Using my uploaded photo as the source image, recreate the exact cinematic lighting, vintage film texture, color grading, and dreamy editorial aesthetic of the reference images.

AESTHETIC: Vintage 1990s Bollywood portrait photography meets intimate, cinematic 35mm film editorial. Moody, romantic, nostalgic, slightly grainy, and softly sensual, resembling a still from an old Indian film shot on analog Kodak film.

LIGHTING: Apply soft, directional tungsten lighting with a warm amber glow illuminating the face from one side. Create gentle highlights across the cheekbones, nose, lips, and forehead, with rich, naturally graduated shadows on the opposite side. Use low-key lighting with subtle chiaroscuro, soft shadow transitions, and a faint atmospheric haze. Avoid harsh overhead lighting, bright studio illumination, or excessive yellow saturation.

COLOR GRADING: Apply a rich, vintage sepia-inspired palette with warm caramel, burnt sienna, muted terracotta, deep chocolate brown, and subtle amber undertones. Introduce slightly desaturated reds, creamy highlights, and warm brownish-black shadows. Reduce blue and green saturation significantly. Maintain natural skin tones underneath the warm grading. Use soft, slightly faded highlights and deep but gently lifted blacks for an authentic analog film finish.

FILM TEXTURE: Recreate the appearance of 35mm Kodak Vision3 500T film with fine-to-medium organic film grain, subtle luminance noise, delicate halation around highlights, and gentle analog softness. Add a slight diffusion filter effect similar to a Black Pro-Mist 1/4 lens filter. Preserve realistic skin texture while introducing subtle film imperfections and an organic, non-digital finish.

FOCUS & OPTICS: Simulate an intimate portrait shot using an 85mm vintage lens at f/1.8. Maintain softly focused facial features with delicate edge diffusion, shallow depth of field, subtle optical bloom, and a dreamy, cinematic softness. Avoid artificial skin smoothing, excessive sharpening, or modern HDR clarity.

CONTRAST & EXPOSURE: Slightly underexpose the overall image by approximately 0.3–0.5 stops. Preserve warm luminous skin highlights while maintaining deep, moody shadows. Apply a soft cinematic S-curve, gently roll off highlights, and retain subtle shadow detail without flattening the image.

IDENTITY PRESERVATION: Keep my exact facial features, facial structure, natural skin tone, ethnicity, body proportions, expression, hairstyle, pose, outfit, jewelry, and all original details completely unchanged. Only transform the lighting, color grading, texture, grain, and photographic atmosphere.

FINAL RESULT: An ultra-realistic, intimate vintage Bollywood film still with warm amber-brown cinematic grading, organic analog grain, soft diffusion, romantic low-key lighting, and beautifully imperfect 1990s film photography aesthetics. The final image should look like an authentic photograph captured on film, NOT a digitally generated or overly retouched portrait.

Change background to plain green wall with color hex code #37321C, keep plain remove anything else in background. 

OUTPUT: High-resolution 9:16 vertical portrait, preserving the original composition and subject identity.

title: A quieter kind of autumn
description: Soft daylight on an empty forest road.
prompt:
Use my uploaded image as the subject reference, preserving my facial features, skin tone, body proportions, hairstyle, and overall identity as faithfully as possible and create an image based on the requirements below.

Prioritize recreating the environment, composition, lighting, depth of field, and photographic mood of the reference image rather than copying the exact outfit or pose.

Background: Position the subject approximately in the center of a wide asphalt road. The road should extend far behind her and gradually curve or disappear into dense greenery, creating strong visual depth and a natural leading line. Surround the road with softly overgrown trees, bushes, and foliage in muted olive, sage, moss, and deep green tones. The ground along both sides should contain scattered dry leaves and subtle brown foliage, suggesting late summer or early autumn. Keep the background natural and uncluttered—no visible buildings, cars, people, signage, poles, fences, or urban elements.

The distant trees and roadway should become progressively softer and more blurred as they recede. Avoid overly lush, saturated tropical greenery; instead use a muted, slightly desaturated woodland palette with hints of olive, dusty green, tan, brown, and faded yellow.

Use approximately an 85mm full-frame equivalent portrait lens, or something in the 70–105mm range, with a moderately shallow depth of field. Keep the subject tack sharp while allowing the road, trees, and foliage behind her to transition into a creamy but still recognizable blur. The depth of field should be shallow enough to separate the subject beautifully, but not so shallow that the environment becomes abstract.

Lighting: Use very soft, natural, diffused daylight, as though photographed during an overcast afternoon or beneath extensive tree cover. The light should wrap evenly around the subject without harsh shadows, blown highlights, or dramatic sunlight. Her face should be softly illuminated from the front and slightly from one side, with delicate dimensionality around the cheekbones and jawline.

Avoid direct golden-hour sunlight, strong rim lighting, hard directional shadows, or visible sunbeams. The lighting should feel quiet, flattering, organic, and almost painterly. Skin should retain natural warmth while the environment remains comparatively subdued.

Color grading: Apply a refined editorial color grade inspired by analog film. Keep greens muted and slightly olive, browns soft and earthy, highlights creamy, and shadows gently lifted. Introduce a subtle warm-neutral cast without making the image overtly yellow or orange. Reduce overall saturation slightly while maintaining realistic skin color.

Aim for soft beige-gray pavement, dusty olive foliage, muted brown leaves, and creamy natural highlights. Maintain gentle tonal contrast rather than crisp digital contrast. Blacks should remain rich but slightly softened rather than crushed.

Photographic texture: The finished image should resemble a professionally photographed fashion editorial using a high-end full-frame camera and premium portrait lens. Preserve realistic skin texture, natural fabric detail, fine hair detail, and subtle environmental texture. Add only an extremely light filmic softness or grain if necessary—nothing visibly vintage, noisy, or artificial.

Keep the overall mood quiet, elegant, contemplative, understated, cinematic, and sophisticated, with the subject feeling naturally integrated into the landscape rather than staged against it.

Important: Do not introduce additional people, vehicles, buildings, artificial props, decorative architecture, flowers, signage, or dramatic scenery. Do not overly beautify or stylize the environment. Keep the road simple, empty, natural, and believable.
